Use the standard Taylor number for an inner cylinder rotating in a stationary outer cylinder, defined as Ta = Ω² R_in d³ / ν², with d = R_out - R_in and ν = μ/ρ.
Convert the rotational speed to radians per second: Ω = 100 rpm × 2π / 60 = 10.4719755 rad/s.
Use R_in = 0.05 m, R_out = 0.052 m, d = 0.002 m, μ = 0.01 Pa·s, and leave ρ as a symbol.
The Taylor number is Ta = Ω² R_in d³ ρ² / μ².
Substituting the values gives Ta = 438.649 × ρ², with ρ in kg/m³.
If ρ is assumed to be 1000 kg/m³, then ν = 1 × 10⁻⁵ m²/s and Ta = 4.386 × 10⁸ rather than the value above.
Wait, recalculate with ν = 1 × 10⁻⁵ m²/s: Ta = Ω² R_in d³ / ν² = 109.662 × 0.05 × 8 × 10⁻⁹ / (1 × 10⁻¹⁰) = 438.649.
So if ρ = 1000 kg/m³, Ta = 438.649.
If ρ is kept symbolic, Ta = 438.649 × ρ².
